paragraphs.text: Dispatch Copilot: launch decision
Launch, packaging and pricing for Q2 2027 · Discussion document for the CEO and executive team
Brightwork
CEO and executive team
Synthetic benchmark data: company and figures are fictional
Executive summary
Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro tier at $12 more per seat, not as a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of new ARR
Copilot is worth launching: it lifts productivity, and Routewise now bundles AI, though the threat is modest
–	Beta accounts lifted jobs per dispatcher-hour 11%, against 2% for matched ones
–	Routewise's AI puts at most $0.64M of new ARR a year at risk
As a $149 add-on, Copilot would earn at most $2.5M of ARR, not $8M, and draw the costliest users
–	Only 14% of beta accounts bought at $149, against 46% who said they would
–	Buyers' inference would absorb 41% of the add-on price
A Pro tier at $12 more per seat earns more, matches Routewise and holds margin with a fair-use cap
–	A third of accounts moving to Pro adds $2.9M, above the $2.3M the NRR target needs
–	Free in Core cuts margin to about 70%; the add-on trails Pro on revenue and fit
The real cost is a two-quarter mobile delay, worth paying only with a gate that can move engineers back
–	Mobile reliability drives 27% of churn, 4.5 times the share for AI features
–	The delay puts up to $1.1M of ARR at risk, on top of $1.47M of engineering

Survey intent overstates demand: 46% said they would buy, but only 14% of beta accounts did when asked to pay
Accounts choosing Copilot at $149 per account per month, % of each group, 2026
Two biases inflate the survey; one limits the paywall
of stated intent turned into purchases
▪	Survey: only 6% of admins replied, and their accounts average 9.4 seats against 6.2 overall
▪	Wording: "likely" and "very likely" both count, and neither commits anyone to pay
▪	Paywall: a real purchase, but by volunteers who were larger and more active than the base, so even 14% is a ceiling
1  Survey: October 2026, 610 of 9,800 account admins. Paywall test: 120 beta accounts offered Copilot at $149 per account per month in the last four weeks of the beta; 17 bought

more ARR a year per account: 6.2 seats × $12 × 12 months

The estimate rests on four assumptions
▪	A third of accounts move within a year, as 33% did when the last higher tier launched in 2023
▪	Accounts that move have the 6.2-seat average; if larger accounts move first, ARR is higher
▪	Lifting NRR from 101% to 105% needs about $2.3M of added net ARR on today's $57.6M
▪	The lift lands in the 12 months after launch; holding 105% after that also needs lower churn (section 4)
Pro's ARR is about 18% above the add-on's best case, and grows with every seat
